catalog_quote: ACENTO El acento generalmente cae en la penúltima sílaba de la palabra. (Una excepción es la palabra /ɑˈri/ ‘sí’.) Por lo tanto, cuando se añade un sufijo, el acento cambia de sílaba: /ˈmɑki/ ‘mano’, /mɑkinˈkunɑ/ ‘sus manos’, /ˈkɑʒbɑj/ ‘corre’, /kɑʒbɑˈɾɑjki/ ‘corriste’, /kɑʒbɑnɢɑˈʒɑpɑ/ ‘correrán’. PALABRA MÍNIMA Y SÍLABA La palabra mínima generalmente tiene dos sílabas si es de clase léxica mayor. Excepciones son: /ˈnɑn/ ‘camino’, /ˈnij/ ‘¡dile! o ¡dí!’, /ˈtɑn/ ‘se sienta’, y /ˈtɑj/ ‘siéntate’. El molde para la sílaba máxima es CVC (con algunas excepciones), y el ataque es obligatorio (excepto en el inicio de la palabra). No hay consonantes extrametricales. Una palabra excepcional con respecto a la estructura silábica de su segunda sílaba es /ɑwˈpɾɑnɑ/ ‘faja de la tejedora’. Palabras con sílabas iniciales especiales son cuatro: /ˈkwiʧkɑ/ ‘demasiado’, /ˈkwɑʃɑ/ ‘triste’, /ˈʧwɑk/ ‘alla’, y…

new_statements.translation: STRESS. Stress generally falls on the penultimate syllable of the word. (One exception is the word /aˈri/ 'yes'.) Consequently, when a suffix is added the stress changes syllable: /ˈmaki/ 'hand', /makinˈkuna/ 'his/her hands', /ˈkaʒbaj/ 'run!', /kaʒbaˈɾajki/ 'you ran', /kaʒbanɢaˈʒapa/ 'they will run'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress on the penultimate syllable of the (suffixed) word; stress is recomputed after suffixation so it always stays on the penult of the whole word. Lexical exception: ari 'yes' with final stress. The same section notes that the minimal major-class word is disyllabic (with a few monosyllabic exceptions such as /ˈnan/ 'road', /ˈtaj/ 'sit!') and that there are no extrametrical consonants.
new_statements.exceptions: /aˈri/ 'sí' has final stress. Independently, Taylor 1982 (Lexis 6(2): 247) notes that Spanish loans with final stress lose it on nativisation (terrón > tirun 'ha perdido la acentuación aguda'), consistent with penultimate stress; Taylor 1982: 268 also mentions 'modificación acentual' in fused clitic sequences without stating a rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (phonological word including suffixes); examples are isolated citation forms in phonemic transcription with stress marks. Author is a native speaker from Inkawasi; recordings from Mamajpampa, Quirichima, Atun Loma, Kañaris, Sinchihual and Inkawasi. The 'generalmente' hedge and the preliminary status of the edition should be noted; the more authoritative descriptions (Escribens 1977, Taylor 1996) could not be opened.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source (Vilcabana Sánchez 2009) describes the Quechua of Inkawasi and Kañaris districts, Ferreñafe province, Lambayeque = lamb1276 (quf) itself; recordings from Mamajpampa, Quirichima, Atun Loma, Kañaris, Sinchihual and Inkawasi. Taylor's work (1982) is based on Ayamachay, Inkawasi district, same language. No dialect-level glottocode distinction needed.
